'''Shannon Leigh Taylor''' (born November 17, 1967) is an American attorney and prosecutor who has served as the [[District attorney|commonwealth's attorney]] for [[Henrico County, Virginia]] since 2012. Taylor was the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee for {{ushr|VA|1}} in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Virginia#District 1|2026 election]]. She [[unseated]] [[Rob Wittman]] in the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2026 |title=Taylor ousts Wittman from Virginia's 1st District in Democratic win |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6189885-shannon-taylor-rob-wittman-virginia-1st-district/ |website=The Hill}}</ref>

Taylor ran in the Democratic primary in the [[2025 Virginia Attorney General election|2025 Attorney General election]], losing the nomination to state delegate [[Jay Jones]].

== Early life and education ==
Taylor was born an raised in [[Charlottesville, Virginia]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Intersections of Violence: Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Child Abuse Conference Biographies|url=https://www.dcjs.virginia.gov/sites/dcjs.virginia.gov/files/training-events/3536/bios.pdf|publisher=Virginia Department of Criminal Justice Services|access-date=November 4, 2026}}</ref> and is an alumnus of [[Albemarle High School (Virginia)|Albemarle High School]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Candidate profiles for the General Election, November 3, 2026 – Gazette Journal |url=https://www.gazettejournal.net/candidate-profiles-for-the-general-election-november-3-2026/ |access-date=2026-10-05 |website=www.gazettejournal.net}}</ref> She graduated from the [[University of Virginia]] in 1989 and earned her [[Juris Doctor]] degree from the [[University of Richmond School of Law]] in 1995.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 5, 2022 |title=Richmond Law Launches New Criminal Justice Forum |url=https://law.richmond.edu/features/article/-/22161/richmond-law-launches-new-criminal-justice-forum.html |website=University of Richmond}}</ref>

== Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney ==
=== Elections ===
On August 11, 2011, Taylor announced her candidacy for the [[2011 Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney election]] with only 11 weeks to go before the election. The office was an open contest as the incumbent, Wade A. Kizer, announced that he would be suspending his candidacy for his fifth term. Her opponent was attorney Matthew Geary, who was a law school classmate and had been campaigning since 2009, and later [[Bill Janis]], who announced his campaign days later.

Taylor won an upset victory over both, receiving 25,975 votes while Janis received 21,540 votes and Geary received 9,045 votes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 9, 2011 |title=In upset, Taylor wins Henrico Commonwealth's Attorney race |url=https://www.nbc12.com/story/15993404/taylor-wins-commonwealths-attorney-race |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=nbc12.com |language=en}}</ref> Some, including Taylor, attributed the win to the split Republican votes between Geary and Janis. Taylor is the first woman to hold the position in Henrico County.

Taylor planned to make the office more diverse and to create cooperation between the office and police. In [[2015 Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney election|2015]], Taylor announced that she would be running for a second term, remaining unopposed in the Democratic primary. She faced prosecutor [[Tony Pham]], who won the Republican primary against Jeffrey Lee Everhart and Shannon Dillon. Pham took aim at Taylor's leadership but ultimately lost in the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Ted |last=Strong |title=Taylor fends off Pham to win second term as Henrico prosecutor |url=https://richmond.com/news/local/government-politics/taylor-fends-off-pham-to-win-second-term-as-henrico-prosecutor/article_db8ad452-c57f-5404-9828-58cc18b1c852.html |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=Richmond Times-Dispatch |language=en}}</ref>

Taylor ran for a third term in [[2019 Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney election|2019]], facing against Owen Inge Conway, a lawyer she fired when she initially took office.<ref>{{Cite web |first=Ali |last=Rockett |title=Henrico's top prosecutor faces challenge from attorney she fired when taking office |url=https://richmond.com/news/local/government-politics/henricos-top-prosecutor-faces-challenge-from-attorney-she-fired-when-taking-office/article_45f15d5b-fa1e-5b62-be18-f4256b620e3f.html |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=Richmond Times-Dispatch |language=en}}</ref> Taylor won against Conway with 62.68% of the vote.

Taylor currently serves as President of the Virginia Association of Commonwealth's Attorneys.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Council and Board Members |url=https://www.vaprosecutors.org/council-and-board-members |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=Virginia Association |language=en}}</ref>

=== Appointment of special prosecutor ===
In 2013, Taylor released a statement that she had requested the judge to appoint a special prosecutor to the case involving [[Joe Morrissey]] and his sexual relationship with a minor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maclauchlan |first=Shawn |date=November 20, 2013 |title=Henrico Commonwealth Attorney releases statement in Morrissey case |url=https://www.nbc12.com/story/24012781/henrico-commonwealth-attorney-releases-statement-in-morrissey-case |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=nbc12.com |language=en}}</ref> Taylor thought that in order for the public to have complete confidence and trust in the proceedings, it was appropriate for decisions to be made by someone outside of Henrico County and that had no prior relationships with the individuals potentially involved.

In 2016, Morrissey exposed himself to a legal client.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2016 |title=Morrissey's campaign continues as he demands RTD retraction |url=https://www.wric.com/news/morrisseys-campaign-continues-as-he-demands-rtd-retraction/ |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=WRIC ABC 8News |language=en-US}}</ref> Taylor began an investigation and later said that although Morrissey was "wrong and unethical" he would not be charged.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2016 |title=Henrico Commonwealth's Attorney on Morrissey: 'Unethical' but no charges |url=https://www.wric.com/news/henrico-commonwealths-attorney-on-morrissey-unethical-but-no-charges/ |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=WRIC ABC 8News |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Police integrity ===
In June 2020, Taylor announced that her office would add a new deputy for police integrity to review police use of force accusations, investigate and review body-worn camera footage, and help determine whether charges are appropriate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 29, 2020 |title=Henrico Commonwealth's Attorney to add new deputy for police integrity |url=https://www.henricocitizen.com/articles/henrico-commonwealths-attorney-to-add-new-deputy-for-police-integrity/ |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=The Henrico Citizen}}</ref> She created it in response to the [[murder of George Floyd]] the previous month, and began looking for a deputy to fill the office. She appointed attorney Misty Whitehead, a [[Black Lives Matter]] supporter, to fill the position, but had funding pulled by County Manager John Vithoulkas after taking issue with private defense attorney Misty Whitehead's social media posts, which included comments about the Breonna Taylor case; questioning her ability – and objectivity – to serve in the role.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Henrico County Manager rescinds funding for police oversight role, questions objectivity of CA's pick |url= https://www.wric.com/news/local-news/henrico-county/henrico-county-manager-rescinds-funding-for-police-oversight-role-questions-objectivity-of-cas-pick/amp/ |access-date=April 1, 2024 |website=wric.com}}</ref>

=== Prosecution of Ku Klux Klan leader ===
On June 7, 2020, a man drove his truck into a crowd of peaceful protesters in Henrico.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ku Klux Klan leader drove truck into crowd of peaceful protesters, Virginia officials say |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/ku-klux-klan-leader-drove-truck-crowd-peaceful-protesters-virginia-n1227691 |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref> The perpetrator was an admitted leader of the [[Ku Klux Klan]]. Taylor announced charges of assault, battery, attempted malicious wounding, and felony vandalism. He was found guilty and sentenced to six years in prison.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Waller |first=Allyson |date=August 11, 2020 |title=Virginia Man, Said to Be a Klan Leader, Gets 6 Years in Prison After Driving Into a Protest |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/08/11/us/kkk-harry-rogers-guilty.html |access-date=April 26, 2023 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

=== Campaign for Attorney General ===
In 2020, there was speculation of whether Taylor would run for the [[2021 Virginia Attorney General election]]. In December 2020, Taylor released a statement that she would not run for attorney general.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eason |first=Hannah |date=December 7, 2020 |title=Henrico commonwealth's attorney announces she will not run for attorney general |url=https://www.nbc12.com/2020/12/06/henrico-commonwealths-attorney-announces-she-will-not-run-attorney-general/ |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=nbc12.com |language=en}}</ref> In January 2021, she announced that she would endorse [[Mark Herring]], the incumbent attorney general.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2021 |title=Henrico Commonwealth's Attorney Taylor endorses Herring |url=https://www.henricocitizen.com/articles/henrico-commonwealths-attorney-taylor-endorses-herring/ |access-date=April 26, 2023 |website=The Henrico Citizen }}</ref>

In 2024, Taylor announced her campaign for Virginia Attorney General. In April 2025, Taylor’s campaign reported over $1 million in donations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=vascope |date=April 5, 2025 |title=Shannon Taylor announces Q1 fundraising haul |url=https://www.virginiascope.com/shannon-taylor-announces-q1-fundraising-haul/ |access-date=June 9, 2025 |website=Virginia Scope |language=en-US}}</ref> The primary was won by [[Jay Jones]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-06-17 |title=Virginia Attorney General Primary Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/06/17/us/elections/results-virginia-attorney-general-primary.html |access-date=2026-08-25 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

== 2026 United States House of Representatives campaign ==
In September 2025, Taylor announced her candidacy for the [[United States House of Representatives]] seat in [[Virginia's 1st congressional district]] in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Virginia|2026 midterm elections]].<ref name=":1">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2025/09/08/virginia-elections-wittman-taylor-congress/|title=Henrico prosecutor joins Democrats aiming to unseat Wittman in Congress|date=September 8, 2025|access-date=January 3, 2026|work=[[The Washington Post]]|author=Schneider, Gregory}}</ref> She had initially announced her campaign for [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Virginia#District 5|Virginia's 5th congressional district]] which had been redrawn after a statewide referendum approved the [[2026 Virginia redistricting amendment]].<ref>{{cite web |author=lowkell |title=Current VA01 Democratic Candidate Shannon Taylor Announces Intention to Run for Redistricted VA05 “upon passage of new maps” |url=https://bluevirginia.us/2026/02/current-va01-democratic-candidate-shannon-taylor-announces-intention-to-run-for-redistricted-va05-upon-passage-of-new-maps/ |access-date=April 21, 2026 |work=BlueVirginia |date=February 6, 2026}}</ref> After the [[Supreme Court of Virginia]] struck down the amendment, Taylor switched her campaign to the 1st district.<ref name=":1" />

On August 4, 2026, Taylor won a majority in the Democratic primary against six other candidates making her the Democratic nominee against incumbent [[Rob Wittman]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2026-08-04 |title=Shannon Taylor wins Democratic primary in Virginia district Democrats hope to make competitive |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/virginia-1st-congressional-district-democratic-primary-results-shannon-taylor/ |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=CBS News |language=en-US}}</ref> She was endorsed in the primary by the [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee]], Governor [[Abigail Spanberger]] and Virginia's senators, [[Mark Warner]] and [[Tim Kaine]].<ref name=":0" />

On November 3, 2026, Taylor flipped Virginia's 1st Congressional District defeating Representative Rob Wittman (R) who held the seat for nearly two decades.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hardy |first=Liana |last2=Government |last3=Reporter |first3=Education |last4=Weinstein |first4=Dina |last5=Reporter |first5=Community Vitality |date=2026-11-04 |title=Taylor unseats Wittman in congressional victory, fueled by overwhelming Henrico support |url=https://www.henricocitizen.com/taylor-unseats-wittman-in-congressional-victory-fueled-by-overwhelming-henrico-support/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=Henrico Citizen |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Swai |first=Finya |date=2026-11-04 |title=Democrat Shannon Taylor poised to flip Virginia's 1st Congressional District |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6189885-shannon-taylor-rob-wittman-virginia-1st-district/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}</ref>
